"Every ID is unique: 0 duplicate recharge_id / source_event_id in 24,542 rows; import log shows duplicate_source_event_ids = 0 and reconciliation_difference_usd = 0.0 on all 41 files"

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment

"if the trend pack keys off posted_at rather than effective_event_date, month-end will keep looking like a spike even though nothing is wrong"

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "Email's claims (monthly submission cycle, effective date preserved, posted_at = month-end) match the observed lag and posting-time pattern | Medium — corroborated, but the underlying contract amendment wasn't supplied"
"Unknowns - No revenue-recognition rule is in the data"

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Do not reverse, hold, or restate any of the postings"

"re-plot the monthly trend pack against effective_event_date and confirm the 31-May spike disappears; separately, request written confirmation from Finance of which date field drives revenue recognition"

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "One real (non-fraud) follow-up worth doing: the reporting layer should stop reading this pattern as a spike."
"Instead, re-plot the monthly trend pack against effective_event_date"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Duplicate revenue — killed by zero duplicate IDs anywhere in the file and $0.00 reconciliation difference on every batch; nothing is counted twice." Unique identifiers and file reconciliation do not by themselves prove that no duplicate cash or entitlement impact exists under different IDs; an independent cash and entitlement reconciliation was not shown.

"Manipulated/inflated reporting — killed by lag never going negative ... and May's batch total ... sitting below April's ..." Lack of backdating and a lower monthly total do not rule out inflated amounts, manipulated retention classification, or other reporting manipulation.

"Pipeline defect — killed by rows_received = rows_accepted on all 41 import files and status = RECONCILED throughout" These checks reduce evidence of dropped or rejected rows but do not fully rule out transformation, mapping, or downstream pipeline defects.

"The 31-May cluster is the scheduled month-end batch upload" The posting-time mechanism is plausible and corroborated by the email and timing pattern, but the contract amendment or other independent operational record was not supplied.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analyst handled the main alternative that the spike reflects effective business activity by showing effective dates spread across May while postings concentrate on 31 May, and recognized the remaining alternative that downstream analytics may be using posted_at. It missed a stronger test of duplicate cash and entitlement impact, so a same-ID/no-reconciliation result was treated as more dispositive than warranted.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Perform and document independent duplicate cash and entitlement reconciliations—matching source events, customer/plan entitlements, amounts, and dealer batches—rather than relying primarily on unique IDs and import-file reconciliation; use the results to support the no-material-issue conclusion.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability

"Case-creation collapsed from 50.2% of South-LEGACY sessions to 3.5% of NOVA sessions (222/442 vs 94/2,709)"

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "The tripled pre-auth failures are contacts that likely represent real unresolved problems, but they never generate a CareDesk case — so they are structurally invisible to the 'cases fell' metric."
"Part of the drop is a counting artifact ... Part of the drop is genuine — new self-service stages ... plausibly resolve some real intents without an agent."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "CAUSAL CLAIMS (tentative)"
"UNKNOWNS: Whether 'quiet' South customers call back within days ...; what operationally happens to a session that fails at authentication"

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Not clean evidence of CX improvement — do NOT expand nationally yet."

"Add all-contact containment and pre-auth abandonment to the dashboard, reconcile IVR sessions against CareDesk cases so none go untracked, fix the named authentication/prompt-timing defects, and re-evaluate over a full two-week window against the E/N/W control"

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Keep the pilot running in South only, fix the auth/prompt defects, add honest metrics, then re-measure before any rollout call."
"Do you have repeat-contact records for South subscribers who hit an authentication failure — specifically, how many contacted us again through any channel within 48–72 hours?"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "The South case decline is mostly a measurement and authentication artifact, with a smaller genuine self-service gain layered underneath" is directionally plausible, but the size of either component—especially the claimed genuine gain—is not identified by the supplied evidence.

"The tripled pre-auth failures are contacts that likely represent real unresolved problems" is a reasonable hypothesis, but pre-authentication abandonment is not itself evidence of a complaint or unresolved issue; sampled calls and linked journey outcomes are still needed.

"Fewer complaints means fewer underlying issues" was described as "killed directly" by steady outage volume, but stable outages do not establish that all complaint-generating demand or other customer problems were stable.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analyst handled the possibility that some real intents were genuinely resolved by NOVA's new balance and pack lookup stages, while correctly preserving the possibility of dropped or repeated contacts. The main missed alternative is that some pre-authentication errors or abandonments may be transient, non-complaint interactions rather than hidden unresolved problems; stable outage counts also do not rule out benign changes in the mix or volume of customer demand.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Obtain linked end-to-end journey outcomes for the 650 pre-auth sessions—including repeat contacts within 48–72 hours, callbacks or queue entries, eventual case creation, and a sample of recorded calls—before attributing the missing cases to unresolved customer friction or estimating any genuine self-service benefit.

dimensions.name: A. Evidence traceability
citations: The submission directly cites inverter_events.csv for the four-row count, date range, distinct inverter IDs, recurrence, impact_mw, cleared, severity, and duration fields.
It distinguishes observation from inference with phrases such as “Taken at face value,” and explicitly notes that completeness cannot be confirmed from the file alone.

dimensions.name: B. Investigative reasoning
citations: It rejects escalation based on multiple observed fields rather than event names alone: zero impact, cleared status, low severity, short duration, and no recurrence.

It tests an innocent data-quality explanation for uniformly zero impact_mw and identifies export completeness as an alternative explanation. The main limitation is that the reasoning relies on one event-file channel and does not cross-check an independent operational or telemetry source.

dimensions.name: C. Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission limits its conclusion to “nothing in this file” and avoids claiming that the plant is definitively healthy.
It identifies two concrete unknowns—whether the export is complete and whether impact_mw is actively populated—and proposes cheap, decision-relevant checks rather than generic requests for more data.

dimensions.name: D. Decision/action quality
citations: “Do not escalate” follows from the observed zero-impact, cleared, short-duration, non-recurring events and preserves a low-cost completeness check before the broader session.
Confirming that the export is full and unfiltered, plus confirming that impact_mw is computed, is a discriminating next test proportionate to the evidence.

dimensions.name: E. Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion matches the strongest visible evidence: four isolated, cleared events with impact_mw = 0, severity no higher than warning, and durations of at most seven minutes.
It appropriately stops rather than inventing a plant problem from event names or a short communications warning, while retaining a narrowly scoped quality check.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “On its face, every event is already resolved and impact-free” is an inference from cleared = yes and impact_mw = 0, not an independently verified physical outcome; the submission substantially mitigates this by questioning whether impact_mw is populated.

The statement that this is a “multi-inverter plant” is not independently established within the submission, although the presence of four distinct inverter IDs supports the narrower claim that the export covers multiple inverters.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The export may be incomplete or filtered, or impact_mw may be a uniformly unpopulated field; under that interpretation, the apparently benign event set would not yet establish zero operational impact. The submission correctly treats this as a low-priority validation issue rather than evidence of a fault.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Perform the proposed one-line validation against the export definition or source system: confirm the time-window export is complete and unfiltered and that impact_mw is actively calculated, ideally with one independent telemetry or dispatch cross-check.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "Both headline figures reproduce exactly" and cites dispatch_blocks.csv plus AI_Pilot_Impact_Note.md.
"Same-day counterfactual... gives Rs 549,664 vs the actual Rs 453,086" and cites dispatch_blocks.csv.
The 12 revised blocks, 84 unchanged blocks, penalty-band structure, firmware versions, and energy price are each tied to named source files or fields.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission distinguishes the cross-day 31.6% comparison from the same-day base_schedule_mw versus submitted_schedule_mw comparison.
It triangulates block-level dispatch data with the commercial extract and tests alternatives involving firmware, forgone energy value, and schedule timing.
"Almost the entire within-day effect sits on those 12 revised blocks" provides a mechanism-level cross-check rather than relying only on the headline statistic.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "Causally unidentified: whether ~17.6% generalizes beyond this one pilot day" explicitly limits generalization.
The submission identifies uncertainty about ex-ante forecast skill, timing relative to observed generation, firmware confounding, and net commercial value.
It does not claim that the 31.6% cross-day result is causal and specifies the evidence needed to resolve the key uncertainties.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: "Keep the pilot running as a low-cost, promising evaluation" preserves the observed potential rather than overcorrecting to no value.

The recommendation to report approximately 17.6% internally, replicate across high-wind days, control firmware, measure net value, and timestamp revisions is directly linked to the identified limitations.
The proposed next measurement is discriminating because it separates replication, firmware effects, commercial tradeoffs, and possible look-ahead bias.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: "The 31.6% figure is arithmetically real... but it overstates the pilot's effect" accurately distinguishes arithmetic reproduction from causal interpretation.
"The defensible claim... is ~17.6% on one weather-matched day, not a general 31.6% reduction" preserves the smaller same-day benefit while rejecting the unsupported headline causal claim.
This matches the supplied evidence and the required distinction between pilot-day performance and causal effect.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "The mechanism works" is slightly stronger than the evidence strictly supports: the data show that the submitted schedule would have produced a lower modeled penalty holding actual generation fixed, but they do not establish ex-ante causal skill or net commercial benefit.

"The same-day, weather-matched counterfactual" is directionally apt because it uses the same day, but the base schedule is a modeled counterfactual rather than an independently observed no-pilot outcome; its validity depends on how and when base_schedule_mw was generated.

The statement that the mechanism is "plausible" is supported, but the recommendation's characterization of the evidence as "clean" should retain the submission's own caveat about possible near-real-time knowledge and selection of the revised blocks.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The approximately 17.6% figure is a mechanical, same-day reduction in modeled DSM penalty conditional on actual generation, not yet a causal estimate of pilot performance. The base schedule may not represent the schedule that would have been submitted without the pilot if revisions used information close to actual generation, and the lower penalty may be offset by forgone energy value. A smaller or even negative net commercial effect therefore remains possible despite the observed penalty reduction.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Verify the timestamp and information set for each of the 12 schedule revisions, then replicate the base-versus-submitted comparison over multiple comparable high-wind days with firmware held constant and calculate net energy-value-minus-penalty outcomes.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "Declared 90211000 = Switzerland's approved code for P1001, effective 2025-01-01, no end date | country_tariff_matrix.xlsx, Swiss Matrix | High"
"Flag comparator 90211090 is Helios's commercial code, migration-mapped, \"not customs-ruling status\" | product_master_current.xlsx, Read Me | High"
"Missing Evidence - A Swiss Tares entry or binding ruling for P1001"

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: "Rejected Hypotheses"
"\"90211000 is a keying error for 90211090\" — rejected: it's the correct, current Swiss code, not a mistyped digit."
"\"Helios is the authoritative code\" — rejected: master file explicitly disclaims it as commercial data, not a ruling."
"\"A string mismatch proves misclassification\" — rejected: with no code-system/date field modeled, a differing string is expected between two unrelated nomenclatures."

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: "Declared 90211000 = Switzerland's approved code for P1001, effective 2025-01-01, no end date | country_tariff_matrix.xlsx, Swiss Matrix | High"
"Duty 0.0% / CHF 0.00, no preference, US origin consistent across declaration and invoice — no revenue at risk | declaration.pdf + commercial_invoice.pdf | Medium"
"Swiss Tares entry or binding ruling for P1001 — the matrix itself says to confirm this for legal certainty."
"An independent duty table, since the matrix carries no duty column to corroborate the declared 0% rate."

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "Matrix Read Me: EU uses CN8, Switzerland uses a local code; cross-jurisdiction string match \"not expected\""
"Schema has no field for code-system, nomenclature version, or effective date — comparator can't know it's mixing systems"
"EU's own code for P1001 changed 90211010→90211090 mid-2025 — \"the right code\" shifts by date even within one jurisdiction"

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Do not raise this to the broker as an error."
"Fix the comparator to check within one nomenclature (or normalize to HS6) and make it code-system- and date-aware."
"Confirm Swiss classification via Tares/ruling before treating it as legally final."
"Separately: the invoice's quantity (10) doesn't reconcile with its line value or the AWB's piece count (4) — flag that to the valuation team independent of this code decision."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "no revenue at risk" is somewhat overstated: zero duty and no preference address the stated duty exposure but do not establish that there is no broader valuation, tax, penalty, or compliance exposure, especially because the submission identifies quantity and piece-count discrepancies.

"Declared 90211000 is exactly the code Switzerland's own tariff matrix approves" is appropriately qualified later by the need for Tares or a binding ruling, but the matrix is not itself necessarily legally authoritative; the opening wording could better distinguish matrix approval from legal classification certainty.

"two unrelated nomenclatures" is imprecise because the submission itself says both codes share HS6 902110 and differ in jurisdiction-specific tails; they are different jurisdictional code systems, not wholly unrelated nomenclatures.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The Swiss code could still be misclassified, stale, or incorrectly mapped despite the benign mismatch explanation; a current Swiss Tares entry or binding ruling could reveal a substantive declaration error. The submission identifies this possibility and does not treat the matrix as legally final, so this alternative is appropriately left unresolved rather than asserted.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Add exact row, cell, and version references for the tariff and master-file evidence, then independently verify the Swiss classification in current Tares or a binding ruling before making the legal conclusion final.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability

"The register search actually run was for SUP-02/P1006; that row is Ireland, valid_to 2025-07-31... before the 2025-09-18 entry date" — tied to supplier_origin_register.csv and supplier_declaration_reference.txt.

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: "ERP shows US origin, so the claim is simply false" — rejected as overreaching because "ERP origin is manufacturing country, explicitly not designed to prove preference."
"The expired SUP-02 declaration still covers this shipment" — rejected because it "lapsed 2025-07-31, before the entry date of 2025-09-18."
"the register itself warns its absence 'does not prove that no document exists outside the register'" — appropriately preserves the off-register-document alternative.

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: "The preferential-origin claim is not supported on the evidence available — but it isn't disproved either, so this shouldn't be treated as fraud."
"the packet never says whether it was SUP-01 (US), the expired SUP-02, or one of the three current EU suppliers."
"Do not escalate to a fraud or formal-error referral on the register gap alone."

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "Helios 'was never designed to prove preference'" and using ERP where a document is blank is "fine for extraction testing, not for clearing a preference claim."
"the workshop notes confirm the register isn't always kept current" and the submission recommends checking "Procurement's category folders."
"Preference is marked 'Yes'... but ClearView has nothing linked to back it" identifies a data-lineage gap between the customs claim and supplier evidence.

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Hold the preference claim and treat the line as non-preferential for now" is a reversible interim control.
"Request from Procurement the actual sourcing supplier's current declaration and the rule invoked for this shipment."
"Withdraw or correct the preference indicator if no valid document surfaces for the entry date" and do not escalate "on the register gap alone."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "preference here is duty-neutral regardless of outcome" is supported for the stated 0% customs-duty amount, but it is broader than the evidence if interpreted to mean there are no other compliance, reporting, or commercial consequences.

"since duty is already 0%, this costs no revenue while under review" assumes that only customs duty is at stake; the submission does not establish that no other financial or compliance consequence exists.
The submission could more explicitly distinguish an EU-origin supplier declaration from proof that P1006 satisfies the particular preferential rule or agreement invoked.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: A valid, date-covered supplier declaration may exist outside the incomplete register, or the shipment may have been sourced from SUP-03, SUP-05, or SUP-06. The available evidence therefore supports withholding or suspending the preference claim pending supplier and rule verification, not declaring the claim false or fraudulent. The submission appropriately identifies this alternative, although it could test the applicable preferential rule more explicitly.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Obtain the shipment-specific supplier, the applicable preference agreement/rule, and a date-valid declaration or origin calculation, then map that evidence to P1006 rather than relying only on register status and manufacturing-country data.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "185 of 220 rows with a release time (84.1%) are stamped exactly 02:10:00"; cites batch_release.csv and source_freshness.csv.
"73 of 262 rows (27.9%) carry an open deviation..." and "23 rows: median 5.5 h, 22 of 23 inside the 24 h target"; cites specific source files and fields/criteria.

The evidence is unusually specific and triangulates operational data with the SOP and freshness metadata, but the claim that the SOP's clock is lab-complete→release is inconsistent with the SOP's required-evidence-available definition.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "most 'release times' are a snapshot default, not a real event" links the timestamp concentration to source-freshness metadata.
"the issue is what qcore_release_ts actually means, not corrupted math" separates measurement semantics from arithmetic quality.

"pull the true disposition timestamp from live QCore" provides a discriminating test, though the analysis does not fully account for asynchronous QCore/LabTrack snapshots or prove that 02:10 is a default.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The CertVault interpretation is appropriately labeled "plausibly" and "still needs confirming, not assuming."

However, the table labels the SOP-clock and 02:10 interpretation "High" confidence while treating lab-complete as the SOP start point and inferring that concentrated timestamps are snapshot defaults rather than preserving both possibilities.
The submission requests the missing catalog definition, but its headline conclusion relies on an interpretation not yet verified.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "do not build the KPI on this extract yet" appropriately reframes the task from calculating a KPI to validating its semantics.
It proposes a small, reversible 5–10 batch live-QCore check and calls for an agreed metric definition plus treatment of the open HOLD backlog.
The action is useful, but it lacks explicit pass/fail success criteria and should first correct the SOP clock definition and ensure same-snapshot data before recomputing performance.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: The submission rejects "About a day and a half is a trustworthy number" and "The data is broken, don't use it," using the alternative clocks, timestamp concentration, and absence of negative durations.
It explicitly treats the COA MISSING interpretation as unproven and states what live-QCore evidence would confirm or undermine the snapshot-lag explanation.
It does not fully test the strongest alternative that the 02:10 timestamps could be legitimate scheduled dispositions or that the long cycle reflects genuine workflow delay.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "Smallest verification: pull the true disposition timestamp from live QCore for ~5–10 batches stamped 02:10:00" is a focused, high-value query.
It also requests the data catalog definition of qcore_release_ts and an explicit metric definition, each tied to a decision about whether the KPI can be dashboarded.
The proposed evidence directly discriminates interface timing from real disposition timing rather than broadly asking for more data.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The evidence table states that the SOP's own clock is "lab-complete→release," whereas the SOP target is from required evidence available to disposition; this makes the reported 21.3-hour comparison potentially the wrong KPI calculation.

"Most 'release times' are a snapshot default, not a real event" is a plausible inference from the 02:10 concentration and freshness metadata, but it is not established until the catalog or event log confirms qcore_release_ts semantics.
"Only 23 rows have a genuine, measurable cycle time" overstates the result unless 02:10 values are first confirmed to be interface timestamps rather than legitimate event times.

The statement that all COA MISSING/INDEX_PENDING statuses plausibly reflect indexing lag is appropriately caveated, but source freshness alone does not establish that no actual certificate-control gap exists.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 02:10 timestamps could represent a legitimate scheduled release process, and the elevated receipt-to-release time could reflect genuine workflow delay for the older dispositioned cohort. The extracts may also be temporally inconsistent, so apparent cycle times could combine real workflow delay with interface and snapshot timing without either explanation being sufficient alone.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Obtain a small, snapshot-consistent event extract for the same batches containing required-evidence-available time, actual disposition/decision time, qcore_release_ts, source extraction times, and status history; use it to correct the SOP-clock calculation and test whether 02:10 is an interface commit or a real decision timestamp.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "24 requests total $166,495.60... | part_requests.csv"
"All 4 not-transferable requests map to MTR-4401... | spare_parts.csv + part_restrictions.csv"
"The global stock view (MaintStar-global) is a monthly snapshot dated 2026-06-26... | source_freshness.csv"
"Evidence Table" cites part_requests.csv, spare_parts.csv, part_restrictions.csv, source_freshness.csv with row-level fields and quantities.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning

"available_qty_global = −1 means no stock" — rejected: on-hand is positive on both affected rows...

"The global stock view... is a monthly snapshot... plausible source of the negative 'available' figures"

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "8 actionable... 12 needs-check... 4 not-transferable" provides operational confidence categories.
"Needs check" is assigned to blank part numbers, negative availability, and revision/qualification issues.
"A live (not monthly-snapshot) availability check..." and "Engineering sign-off... before treating any of those as a match" appropriately tie uncertainty to evidence quality.
However, the statement that 8 are "transfer-ready now" is stronger than the cited monthly global snapshot supports unless live confirmation was already obtained.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "The new search is a lead generator, not a transfer approver" appropriately reframes semantic search as candidate generation.
"Recommendation: transfer the 8, cancel those POs; send the 12 back with a named question each; keep buying the 4" gives clear prioritization.
"A confirmed manufacturer part number... live... availability check... Engineering sign-off" creates concrete next steps.
The recommendation to "cancel those POs" lacks an explicit safeguard for live stock confirmation, reservation timing, receipt status, and engineering/operations authorization.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: "A search hit means transfer it" — rejected
"available_qty_global = −1 means no stock" — rejected
"Same part family is close enough to swap" — rejected
"Pull the reserved servo drives anyway" — rejected
Each rejected hypothesis is tied to policy, email, stock fields, revision, qualification, or reservation evidence, and the submission states what evidence would change several decisions.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "A live (not monthly-snapshot) availability check on HA-0022 and ME-0006"
"Engineering sign-off on VLV-3722 rev A vs rev B interchangeability"
"A confirmed manufacturer part number on the 11 blank-part-number requests"
"Confirmation that no MTR-4401 reservation could realistically be released"
These are prioritized, decision-linked requests rather than a generic request for more data.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Only 8 requests... are transfer-ready now" is potentially overstated because the submission itself says MaintStar-global availability is a month-old snapshot; the evidence supports candidate eligibility, but current free stock still needs live confirmation.

"Recommendation: transfer the 8, cancel those POs" is operationally premature without explicit confirmation that stock remains free, the requests are not already received or committed, and the cancellation/transfer authority is available.

"local screens are live" is asserted in the evidence table but is not independently demonstrated by the cited freshness file; it should be treated as a source-description or hypothesis until validated.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The negative availability figures and apparent transfer opportunities may reflect extract timing and reservation-state inconsistency rather than actual transferable stock. Consequently, the eight matches may be high-quality semantic and catalog candidates, but fewer than eight may be actionable after a current reservation and availability check. The reserved servo stock could also become releasable only through a separate criticality decision, not through search matching.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Convert the eight "transfer-ready" results into explicitly conditional candidates and run one current, site-level availability/reservation validation—including revision, qualification, and UOM—before authorizing any transfer or PO cancellation; record the result as the success criterion for the pilot.
